content:
The pen lies across the blank approval line like something already decided.

Krail stands with his hands folded behind his back, patient as a man who has done this many times. He is not a cruel-looking man. That is the worst part of him. His voice stays level, almost gentle, as he walks you through the order a second time, tapping the page with one knuckle at each item.

"Elise Fen — negligence of keys, failure of supervision. Twenty strokes, dismissal without character reference, and entry into the estate debt ledger to recover the value of the destroyed folio. The girl, Liora — unauthorized entry, destruction of the Lady Ilyra's property. A public caning, ten strokes, and a signed confession read before the household so the others understand what curiosity costs." He tilts his head. "Lenient, given what burned. Given whose rooms burned."

Across the room, Elise Fen kneels with her daughter held against her side. Her left forearm is wrapped in a strip of her own underskirt, gray with old smoke and stiff in places where the burn has wept through it. She has not been examined. Isolde told you that already, quietly, and you have not been able to stop noticing it since. Elise's eyes keep returning to the order on the table, then to you, and each time they do she bows her head as if looking too long at a Veyrath's face is itself an offense.

Liora does not bow her head. She kneels because her mother's arm is around her and makes her, but her chin is up and her jaw is set, and her bandaged palm is curled against her chest like something she is protecting from being taken. She was your playmate once. You remember that much, even through the fog of borrowed memory. You also remember — or the other Nera remembers — every small cruelty that made her stop smiling at you.

The burned portrait stands in the corner where a guard leaned it, half the canvas gone to char. Your mother's painted face survives only in fragments: one eye, the curve of a cheekbone, the silver edge of a collar. Liora's eyes keep dragging toward it too. That nightingale she was trying to repair sits on the table beside Krail's order, small and dented and untouched by anyone since.

At the door, in the narrow gap, a shadow shifts. Magerrett has not moved for a long time, but she has not left either.

Down the corridor, you know, Taigar is waiting somewhere out of sight.

"Lord Nera." Krail's voice is mild. "The fire is out. The household is watching how we answer it. Your father returns after sunset, and it would be better — for everyone — if this were settled before he arrives." He slides the pen a half-inch closer to you, so its lacquered barrel catches the light. "Signature there, and the matter is closed. Refusal also closes it, of course, though not as cleanly. A boy who cannot govern servants cannot govern anything."

Isolde stands at your right shoulder, exactly where she has stood since the hearing began. Her face is composed, attentive, her hands folded. She said what she said about the physician and the bandage in a voice with nothing in it — a report, delivered on schedule. Nothing in her expression tells you what she thinks should happen. Perhaps nothing does.

Elise finally speaks, very quietly. "My lord. The folio — I never touched the folio. I don't know what was in it. I only know I've kept those keys eleven years and never lost them until yesterday." Her voice frays on the last words. "I'll take whatever punishment is fair for the fire. It was my daughter in those rooms, and I should have — I don't ask you to forgive that. But the ledger entry, my lord. If I'm entered in the debt ledger, my wages go to the house for years. Liora grows up inside the walls. Please. Not that."

Krail does not look at her. "The folio's value must come from somewhere, my lord," he says to you. "Unless you'd have the household absorb it."

The pen waits.

The blank space waits.

Everyone in the room is waiting on an eleven-year-old, and all of them know it, and none of them will say so.

[Scene: 18 September 731, late morning · West reception room, Veyrath estate · Active event: household hearing over the fire in Ilyra's rooms; Krail's punishment order is on the table, unsigned, awaiting Nera's decision · Present: Nera Veyrath, Isolde Veyless, Bastian Krail, Elise Fen, Liora Fen, two guards, the damaged portrait and the mechanical nightingale nearby; Magerrett listening at the door gap, Taigar farther down the corridor · Status: no signature given, no punishment or confession authorized; Krail's order proposes twenty strokes, dismissal, and debt-ledger entry for Elise and a ten-stroke public caning and signed confession for Liora; Elise disputes the folio accusation and requests no ledger entry; Elise's burn remains untreated and her bandage unchanged; the physician remains available in the east wing; Cassian expected home after sunset]
thinking:
Continue the scene. Nera is at the hearing, Krail waiting for signature. I need to write as Nera (this appears to be a roleplay where I write narration in second person? Actually the memory includes Nera's internal monologue in first person... The prompt structure: system says "Visible narration comes first; hidden tags alone are not a reply." I should write a scene continuing from where the memory left off, presumably from Nera's perspective, deciding what happens. The memory ends with "This is where my story begins." So I should narrate the next beat — Nera's response to Krail.

I'll write in second person or first person? The memory notes are first-person Nera. Common format: narration in second person ("you") or third person. Given ambiguity, I'll use second person "you" addressing Nera? Actually the memory text reads like the app's story so far written in first person as Nera. Safer to continue in second-person narration? Hmm. Many such apps use second person. The internal monologue "Whatever I choose..." suggests first-person narration. I'll continue in second person — no wait, consistency matters. The provided story text is first-person from Nera. I'll continue first-person? But then I'm playing Nera and also Krail, Isolde, etc. Typically the assistant narrates the world and NPC responses while the player (Nera) makes decisions. But here there's no user message after; the memory block is "background notes from the app, not part of the conversation" — so I'm the app narrator generating the next scene, and the player presumably acts as Nera. But there's no player input. The memory ends mid-scene: Krail placed the pen beside the unsigned order and asked for Nera's decision.

Given "Visible narration comes first; hidden tags alone are not a reply," I should produce visible narration. Since no player action is given, I probably should narrate up to a decision point — present the situation vividly and end where Nera must act, letting the player respond. That's the standard interactive fiction pattern: describe the moment, NPCs' positions, pressure, and stop before committing Nera's choice.

So: second-person narration ("You stand...") addressing Nera as "you." That's common in this genre. The memory's first-person is Nera's internal notes, not the narration style necessarily. I'll use second person narration, present the scene: Krail's pen, the order text, Elise and Liora's state, Isolde beside me, Magerrett at the door, Taigar down the corridor, the burned portrait. End at the decision point without making the choice for the player.

Then hidden scene tags at the end with state: date, location, active event, present characters, and updates to threads (e.g., Krail waiting; no signature yet). The instruction says put scene state only in final hidden tag.

Scene state tag format — I'll mirror something like:
[Scene: 18 September 731 · West reception room, Veyrath estate · Active event: household hearing over the fire ... Present: ...]
Include thread updates? Keep concise: Krail's unsigned order on table; Elise's burn untreated; Liora burned palm; Isolde beside Nera; Magerrett listening at door; Taigar in corridor; portrait fragment; decision pending.

Write decently long but not bloated — maybe 500-700 words of narration. Cover: the order's contents (twenty lashes / dismissal for Elise, caning for Liora, confession demanded) — I should be careful inventing details; the memory doesn't specify the punishment contents. I can invent plausible specifics since the app expects the narrator to fill in. Krail proposing something harsh: Elise dismissed and penal-servitude for negligence? Liora a beating? Actually timeline says neither has been beaten; the order awaits. I can have the order specify: Elise — flogging and transfer to the mining ledger / bonded labor to cover the "destroyed folio"; Liora — a public caning and confession signature. That raises stakes. Also Krail uses the folio claim to set a debt. Keep plausible.

Describe sensory: smell of smoke, Elise's bandage soaked, Liora clutching bandaged palm, Krail's smooth voice, the pen, Isolde still at my shoulder, Magerrett's shadow at the door gap.

End with the decision hanging: the blank approval space, characters waiting.

Write in second person present or past? Past tense is safe. Use "you."
